source.post_text:
Introducing Muse Code (beta), a terminal coding agent built for long-horizon software engineering, powered by our new Muse Spark 1.2 model.

Muse Code plans, implements, and validates complex, multi-file changes across large repositories with persistent sub-agents that solve difficult problems faster, more accurately, and with less intervention.

🧵👇

replies.text: The persistent sub-agents + append-only event log design looks like a real step forward for long-running agent reliability. Curious how well it handles mid-task recovery on messy real-world repos.
replies.author: @freesouleth

replies.text: the thing nobody says out loud: sub-agents that persist are just procrastination with extra steps.
replies.author: @hass_avocado_

replies.text: Congrats! I'm cheering for you Meta.
replies.author: @zook_data

replies.text: Persistent sub-agents for multi-file work could cut down on context loss quite a bit, though success still hinges on how cleanly they hand off state without drifting. Worth watching how Muse Spark 1.2 performs once people throw real messy repos at it.
replies.author: decoy

replies.text: Long-horizon coding is less about writing more code and more about keeping a clean state. The activity log, resumability and ability to explain why a file changed may matter as much as benchmark scores. A fast agent that forgets its plan is still expensive.
replies.author: @eyitayo4u2

decoy_rationale: The reply is oddly balanced and slightly explanatory in a hedged way that feels more composed than casual.
